summary:
THREE ITEMS, ALL RE-VERIFIED AGAINST THE CURRENT TREE BEFORE ANY EDIT. Item 1 reproduced exactly as re-framed and is FIXED. Item 2 reproduced and is FIXED. Item 3 was a decision, and carrying it out REFUTED the premise it was handed to me with: the ordinary tidy-up breaks ONE producer, not five, measured on a scratch tree in both directions.

ITEM 1. src/spine/assemble.py::COUPLINGS' CAP.d_expert_slots row said capacity/levers.py "records that it is absent from this table"; that file's module docstring today says the opposite in capitals ("ALL FOUR WIRES NOW EXIST IN spine/assemble.py's COUPLINGS"), so the coupling row was the stale side. The claim was carried as a bare `:123`, and `sed -n '123p' src/capacity/levers.py` is a BLANK LINE -- the citation pointed at nothing even in the revision where the sentence was true. The sibling CAP.d_vocab_slots row's `:244` lands inside the fab_start comment. Both rows now cite symbols: capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers.fab_start and capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers.vocab_start, each verified to contain the sentence attributed to it. The row also now records that it asserted the opposite, and why that direction costs. docs/04_CONTRACT.md lines 70 and 71 carry the identical pair of dangling citations and are NOT mine: the exact find/replace is under unfinished.

ITEM 2. spine/compose.py::compose called sig_api.warm_up as a BARE EXPRESSION STATEMENT and the WarmupReport went on the floor, while the ASSEMBLY_ORDER row four hundred lines above said "it is a WarmupReport the root must act on itself". The return is now bound to a new System slot `warmup`, and a verdict of 'collapsing' puts a line on System.warnings carrying separation_final, separation_peak, steps and probes. NO POLICY WAS INVENTED: neither sig/api.py::warm_up nor docs/04_CONTRACT.md says what acting on the verdict IS, so the code does not refuse the run and does not raise, and the warning line SAYS it is a carrier and not a classification -- both alternatives are named in the comment above it with what each would cost. Exercised by lifting the shipped `if` out of compose.py by AST and running it against real WarmupReports: 'collapsing' -> 1 warning with the numbers in it; 'plateau', 'budget' and a stub's None -> 0.

ITEM 3, AND THE PREMISE IS WRONG. The referral said adding `__slots__ = ()` to units.py's six Clock kinds "BREAKS all five producers". MEASURED: a scratch copy of src/ with exactly that edit breaks CKPT.save_period ('Windows' object has no attribute 'gates') and NOTHING ELSE -- CAP.new_valve, FAB.build, MEM.open_store, SIG.build and TOK.build_vocabulary all still return their gates, because none of the five is a Clock subclass: FAB's Population, MEM's Store and TOK's Vocabulary name 'gates' in their OWN __slots__, and CAP's Valve and SIG's SigState carry their own __dict__. Exactly one producer stands on the omission. RULED: the affordance is now DECLARED -- spine/units.py::Clock carries `__slots__ = ("n", "gates")` with a docstring paragraph naming D14, the one producer, and the value-object caveat -- and the six kinds carry the tidy-up `__slots__ = ()` themselves, so the edit that used to break the tree is the state it ships in. spine/units.py::_verify_gate_channel runs at IMPORT and refuses both regressions by name: removing 'gates' from the slot list, and deleting a kind's `__slots__ = ()` (which would put the implicit __dict__ back and make the channel an accident again). Both refusals were triggered on scratch trees. All six producers re-run green afterwards, and the instances got SMALLER: a bare Windows 64 -> 48 bytes, a gated one 352 -> 48.

findings.detail: DEFECT_CONFIRMED, not already fixed. The CAP.d_expert_slots row's `why` read 'capacity/levers.py::<module> names this exact field as what CAP_FAB_START's 0 sentinel resolves to and :123 records that it is absent from this table.' The first clause is true and stays. The second is false in substance -- src/capacity/levers.py's module docstring now reads 'ALL FOUR WIRES NOW EXIST IN spine/assemble.py's COUPLINGS and every one of them is read by a body or a stub in capacity/api.py', and records that it said the opposite for several commits and was corrected on 2026-09-03. It is also false in form: ':123' is a BLANK LINE in the current tree. The row now cites src/capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers.fab_start for the sentinel and src/capacity/levers.py::<module> for the four-wires sentence, states that this row carried the opposite claim until 2026-09-04, and says why an absence asserted about a declared row costs (it tells the next porter to ADD four couplings the table already has). THE SIBLING ROW WAS THE SAME DEFECT AND IS FIXED IN THE SAME EDIT: CAP.d_vocab_slots cited ':244', which today lands inside the fab_start comment; it now cites src/capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers.vocab_start, whose comment block says in as many words that 'TOK holds no ceiling of its own to give'. NO COUPLING WAS ADDED, REMOVED OR RETARGETED: src and dst and compute are untouched, so the ledger is unchanged at 23 couplings / 19 wires / 4 intra-package against WIRE_BUDGET=25 -- test_assemble A8 prints exactly those numbers after the edit. docs/03_WIRING.md is generated from render() and was regenerated with the tool test_assemble A9 itself names; the diff is 4 lines, all of them these two `why` strings.
findings.repro: BEFORE: `grep -n ':123' src/spine/assemble.py` -> the CAP.d_expert_slots row; `sed -n '123p' src/capacity/levers.py` -> a blank line; `sed -n '244p' src/capacity/levers.py` -> '# 4096 (FAB_NMAX's default, now FAB_SLOTS). The arms set it deliberately and across a wide range --', i.e. the fab_start comment, not anything about d_vocab_slots. `grep -n 'ALL FOUR WIRES NOW EXIST' src/capacity/levers.py` -> line 134. AFTER: `python3 tests/test_assemble.py` -> '9 checks, 0 failing' with A8 reading 'live tree: 262 levers in 13 packages, 23 couplings, wire budget 25' and A9 '239 generated line(s) compared'; `python3 tests/test_couplings.py` -> '4 checks, 0 failing'; `python3 tests/test_ownership.py` -> '12 checks + 18 self-test cases, 0 failing', which is O12 resolving the two new symbol citations.

findings.detail: DEFECT_CONFIRMED, not already fixed. `sig_api.warm_up(...)` was a bare expression statement -- the only warm_up call site in the file -- so the WarmupReport was computed and dropped. sig/api.py::WarmupReport's own docstring: "'collapsing' is a RUN-LEVEL FAILURE and NO signature in this tree takes it as an argument: this record is what the composition root has to act on itself"; compose.py's own ASSEMBLY_ORDER row repeated the sentence over the discarding call. THE FIX. (a) System gains a `warmup` slot, with a comment saying why it is NOT a `produces` column (no later row consumes it) and NOT one of the four cross-boundary carriers (it is a result the root owns). (b) the call binds: `sysm.warmup = sig_api.warm_up(...)`. (c) a 'collapsing' verdict appends one line to System.warnings carrying separation_final, separation_peak, steps and probes, and naming what is downstream of a collapsed encoder. (d) the ASSEMBLY_ORDER row now says the return is bound and where. WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND IT IS THE POINT. sig/api.py::warm_up and docs/04_CONTRACT.md both say the verdict is a run-level failure and NEITHER says what acting on it is, so no policy was invented: appending to System.refusals would make a collapsed encoder abort the run and raising would kill it before the report that carries the numbers prints -- both are rulings. Both are named in the comment with their costs, and the warning line itself says 'THIS ENTRY IS A CARRIER AND NOT A POLICY', so nobody can read 'the root acted' off a warnings entry that only forwards the verdict. The report object is on System.warmup for whoever rules.
findings.repro: BEFORE: the call at compose.py's `warmup` stage was `sig_api.warm_up(sig, sysm.sig, ...)` with no assignment target -- confirmed by AST (an ast.Expr, not an ast.Assign). AFTER, with the shipped `if` lifted out of compose.py BY AST and executed against real WarmupReports (scratch script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/cspine/warmup_reader.py): verdict='collapsing' (peak 0.16, final -0.0, 500 steps, 1 probe) -> 1 warning, beginning 'RUN-LEVEL FAILURE, not a warning: SIG.warm_up returned verdict=...'; verdict='plateau' -> 0; verdict='budget' -> 0; a stub returning None -> 0. K2 (compose imports and builds against the stubs, raising nothing but NotImplementedError) still passes: test_contract reports 14 checks with only K12 failing, and K12 was already failing before I touched anything.

findings.detail: THE RULING, CARRIED OUT. `Clock.__slots__` is now `("n", "gates")` and each of the six kinds carries `__slots__ = ()`. The Clock docstring gains a paragraph that names the channel, names D14 and the ONE producer that uses it (ckpt/api.py::save_period), states that it used to work by an omission, and states what declaring it does NOT fix -- the slot is unset on a fresh instance and every operation returns a fresh instance, so `period - Windows(1)`, `Windows(period)` and `period + Windows(0)` still come back with no gates, exactly as when the carrier was a __dict__; a reader must use `getattr(clock, 'gates', ())` and a caller must not re-wrap a period it was handed. NOTHING units.py EXISTS FOR MOVED: Steps(1) >= period still raises UnitError, period == 0 still raises, int/index/bool/str/repr/hash are unchanged and a gated Windows still hashes equal to a bare one. TWO THINGS GOT BETTER BESIDES. (i) a Clock now refuses an UNDECLARED attribute -- `period.undeclared = 1` raises AttributeError where the implicit __dict__ used to accept anything at all on a value object. (ii) instances shrank: a bare Windows 64 -> 48 bytes, a gated one 352 -> 48 (sys.getsizeof, old module and new module loaded side by side), because the declared slot REPLACES a __dict__ pointer plus a lazily created dict rather than adding to it. So the stated cost of the option -- 'a report channel on a value object six kinds share' -- is 8 bytes that were already being spent, and is paid only against a measured saving.
findings.repro: python3 -c on the tree: 'attach ok: ("g",) | dict: False'; 'undeclared attribute REFUSED: Windows object has no attribute anything'; 'UnitError intact: yes -- >=: Steps against Windows'; pickle round-trips. ALL SIX .gates PRODUCERS CALLED LIVE (scratchpad/cspine/producers_live.py, plus TOK.build_vocabulary over the real corpus): CKPT.save_period 1 gate (Windows), CAP.new_valve 2 (Valve), FAB.build 2 (Population), MEM.open_store 1 (Store), SIG.build 0 (SigState, a dict populated later), TOK.build_vocabulary 1 (Vocabulary). The five period accessors all still return units.Windows: CKPT 0 with its gate, EVAL 2000, DOM 100, FAB 500, MEM 200. Suite: ownership 12/0 failing, assemble 9/0, couplings 4/0, census 7/0, derive 575 oracle cases 0 mismatches.

findings.detail: THE REQUIRED OUTCOME -- that someone adding __slots__ next year FAILS A CHECK rather than silently breaking DID IT FIRE reporting -- is met in two layers, because I may not touch tests/**. Layer one: the tidy-up is already applied, so the specific edit that used to break the tree cannot be made again. Layer two: a module-level check that runs at IMPORT and refuses BOTH ways the declaration can go wrong. (a) if any kind can no longer take `.gates` -- someone trims Clock.__slots__ back to ('n',), or shadows it -- it raises naming D14, naming CKPT.save_period, and naming the repair. (b) if any kind carries a __dict__ again -- someone deletes a `__slots__ = ()` -- it raises too, because the channel would then work by accident once more and any attribute at all could be hung on a value object. AN IMPORT CHECK AND NOT A TEST, for a stated reason: this file is imported by every package and every tool, so the failure reaches whoever made the edit on the next thing they run, and an import cannot be run selectively. It does not replace a test in tests/**, and the docstring says so.
findings.repro: Two scratch trees under scratchpad/cspine/. drop_slot (Clock.__slots__ trimmed to ('n',)): `python3 -c 'import spine.units'` -> RuntimeError: 'spine.units.Steps can no longer carry `.gates`. That attribute is the DID IT FIRE channel decision D14 shipped CKPT.save_period on ... Restore 'gates' to spine/units.py::Clock's __slots__'. restore_dict (Windows' `__slots__ = ()` deleted): -> RuntimeError: 'spine.units.Windows instances carry a __dict__ again, so `.gates` is once more an ACCIDENT rather than the declared slot ... Give every kind in CLOCK_KINDS `__slots__ = ()` back'. The real tree imports clean and the whole suite runs.

findings.detail: THE REFERRED FRAMING IS WRONG AND THE NUMBER MATTERS, because it is the number the ruling was supposed to turn on. The referral -- and ckpt/api.py's own cost-(2) paragraph, which is where it comes from -- says adding `__slots__ = ()` to the six kinds 'turns this function's last-but-one statement into an AttributeError, AND DOES THE SAME TO THE FOUR SIBLING PRODUCERS NAMED ABOVE'. It does not. The four siblings plus SIG attach `.gates` to their OWN record objects and none of those is a Clock subclass, so nothing in spine/units.py can reach them: FAB's Population, MEM's Store and TOK's Vocabulary each name 'gates' in their own __slots__ (a declared affordance already), and CAP's Valve and SIG's SigState declare no __slots__ at all and so carry their own __dict__. EXACTLY ONE PRODUCER STANDS ON THE OMISSION: CKPT.save_period. This does not make the trap smaller in kind -- one silently lost gate is the whole class of defect spine/gate.py exists to refuse -- but a ruling written against 'five packages break' would have been a ruling against a measurement nobody took. The correcting edit to ckpt/api.py is under unfinished; that file is another agent's.
findings.repro: A scratch copy of src/ with `__slots__ = ()` inserted into all six kinds (scratchpad/cspine/tidyup), run through scratchpad/cspine/producers_live.py: 'CKPT.save_period RAISED AttributeError: 'Windows' object has no attribute 'gates'' while CAP.new_valve, FAB.build, MEM.open_store and SIG.build all returned their gates unchanged. Statically: `Clock subclass: False` for all five record classes, and 'gates' in FAB.Population.__slots__ / MEM.Store.__slots__ / TOK.Vocabulary.__slots__ is True.

It does NOT touch the four sibling producers named above, nor SIG: none of them is a Clock subclass -- Population, Store and Vocabulary name `gates` in their own __slots__ and Valve and SigState carry their own __dict__ -- so this function is the ONLY producer that stands on units.py.'

D11 FORM, so it can be pasted as the next D-number.
TITLE: A Clock's `.gates` channel is DECLARED, and its removal fails at import.
WHAT WAS READ OR RUN: src/spine/units.py, src/ckpt/api.py::save_period and D14; every `.gates` assignment in src/ (six, at capacity/api.py:436, ckpt/api.py:256, fabric/api.py:460, memory/api.py:186, sig/api.py's dict writes and tok/api.py:416); the __slots__ of Population, Store, Vocabulary, Valve and SigState by AST; a scratch tree with the tidy-up applied, run through all six producers; two further scratch trees for the two regressions; sys.getsizeof on the old and new modules loaded side by side.
ALTERNATIVES AND WHY THEY LOST. (A) `__slots__ = ()` on the six kinds, the ordinary tidy-up. REFUSED ALONE: it removes CKPT.save_period's shipped Gate with no error at the producer -- that is the quiet narrowing, and D14 shipped that gate yesterday. (B) Leave the omission and change nothing. REFUSED: a mechanism that works because of what nobody wrote is the shape this project refuses everywhere else, and it has a plausible trigger -- the tidy-up is what a reader who has never seen D14 would do. (C) Leave the omission and add only a check. REJECTED as second-best: it makes the break loud but keeps the affordance undeclared, so the check is guarding an accident rather than a contract, and a reader of units.py still finds no statement that a Clock carries gates. (D) `__slots__ = ('gates',)` on each of the six kinds. REJECTED on placement, not on substance: it says every kind is a report carrier six times over, when the convention is the Clock's -- today only Windows carries a gate, and every period accessor returns a Clock. (E) Widen CKPT.save_period's return to a (Windows, Gate) pair or a record. ALREADY REFUSED BY D14 and it touches spine/compose.py and docs/04_CONTRACT.md.
CHOSEN: `Clock.__slots__ = ('n', 'gates')` -- one named declaration in the class the convention belongs to -- plus `__slots__ = ()` on the six kinds, plus spine/units.py::_verify_gate_channel refusing at import in BOTH directions.
COSTS AND WHAT IT FORECLOSES. A `gates` slot exists on five kinds that do not use one: 8 bytes each, and they were already being spent on a __dict__ pointer -- measured, a bare Windows went 64 -> 48 bytes and a gated one 352 -> 48, so this is cheaper than what it replaces. A Clock can no longer take an undeclared attribute, which is a tightening but would break any future code that hung something else on a clock; that code must declare it. It does NOT fix the real remaining hazard, which is that arithmetic returns a fresh instance and drops the tuple -- and it should not: propagating report state through a value object's arithmetic is a bigger ruling than this one.
WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: a second producer attaching to a Clock kind other than Windows would confirm the base-class placement; a consumer that must read `.gates` off a clock AFTER arithmetic would reopen the drop-on-re-wrap question and push toward (E) after all; and a decision to give CKPT a package-wide DID IT FIRE accessor (already referred in ckpt/api.py, needing docs/04_CONTRACT.md and spine/compose.py together) would retire the attachment entirely.
ALSO WORTH RECORDING IN THE ENTRY: the referral said this edit broke FIVE producers. It breaks one.
